title_en: The ETF Graveyard: This Has Been a Record Year for Closures
title_zh: ETF 墓地：清盘数量创纪录的一年
subtitle_zh: 彭博 Trillions 播客“ETF 墓地”万圣节特辑，主持人 Joel Weber、Eric Balchunas 携手 Baird Strategas 的 Todd Sohn 与彭博行业研究的 Andre Yap，盘点2026年创纪录的 ETF 清盘潮与那些可能被“复活”的产品。
summary_zh: 本期 Trillions 是万圣节常设特辑'ETF 墓地'（ETF Graveyard），Joel Weber 与 Eric Balchunas 携手 Baird Strategas 首席 ETF 策略师 Todd Sohn 和 Bloomberg Intelligence 高级 ETF 研究专员 Andre Yap，盘点本日历年的清盘潮。Balchunas 给出宏观数据：历史上约发行 8000 只 ETF、已有约 2500 只清盘，'每三四只就有一只会消亡，而且死得越来越年轻'；Yap 补充 2026 年正走向清盘数量创纪录的一年，目前 245 只并列历史第三，年底或达约 250 只。清盘集中在几类：大量 ESG 基金（连'能把冰卖给爱斯基摩人'的 Schwab 都关掉）、刚出生就夭折的两倍杠杆个股 ETF（Tradr、T-Rex、Defiance 等）、以及边缘加密货币和股票型基金。Sohn 惋惜一些独特产品消失，如 BondBloxx 按行业拆分高收益债的系列（XHYF、XHYH 等），认为它们是观察超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）债务承压的绝佳工具；Balchunas 则谈到反复'复活'又清盘的 KraneShares 全球奢侈品 ETF（KLXY）。节目还讨论了'流动性最好那只才活得下来'的杠杆产品逻辑、Corgi 低费率却无人问津的困境，以及各自的'复活'候选，如 AdvisorShares 酒店 ETF（BEDZ）、Themes 自然垄断 ETF（CZAR）与两倍做多农产品的 CORX、WHTX。
description: The ETF Graveyard: This Has Been a Record Year for Closures

turns.en: Bloomberg Audio Studios. Podcasts. Radio. News.
turns.zh: 彭博音频工作室（Bloomberg Audio Studios）。播客。电台。新闻。

turns.en: I think you'll see more culling of those lineups, but more piling into tech, because that's where the assets are going. There's a 2X Starbucks. I'm drinking a pumpkin spice coffee right now. I don't need 2X of that.
turns.zh: 我觉得你会看到这些产品线被进一步精简，同时资金会更多地涌向科技板块，因为资产正在往那里流。市面上甚至有一只2倍杠杆的星巴克ETF。我这会儿正喝一杯南瓜香料咖啡，可我不需要“2倍”的它。

turns.en: Welcome to Trillions. I'm Joel Webber.
turns.zh: 欢迎收听 Trillions。我是乔尔·韦伯（Joel Weber）。

turns.en: And I'm Eric Balchunas.
turns.zh: 我是埃里克·巴尔丘纳斯（Eric Balchunas）。

turns.en: Eric, it's Halloween season, which means one of our ongoing episodes is ETF Graveyard, dedicated to funds that have closed this calendar year.
turns.zh: 埃里克，现在是万圣节季，这意味着我们的常设节目之一“ETF 墓地（ETF Graveyard）”又回来了，专门盘点本日历年度内已经清盘的基金。

turns.en: Yeah, and the graveyard is getting big.
turns.zh: 是啊，而且这座墓地越来越大了。

turns.en: Really?
turns.zh: 真的吗？

turns.en: Really big, yeah.
turns.zh: 真的很大，没错。

turns.en: Just for those... I guess there's a lot of ETFs, so that means the graveyard's got to get big too.
turns.zh: 跟大家说一下……我想现在 ETF 数量很多，所以墓地自然也会越来越大。

turns.en: Roughly speaking, there's been 8,000 ETFs launched and 2,500 have closed now. So the graveyard is 2,500 big. Basically, one of every three or every four ETFs is going to die. And now they're dying younger. And so it's good to look through here. A, what is caught our attention? Are there any that we felt should have made it and didn't? Are there any trends that we see? It's just interesting. And And are there any that will try to get dug up and resurrected Lazarus style?
turns.zh: 粗略地说，历史上大约发行了8000只 ETF，如今已有2500只清盘。所以这座墓地里有2500座坟。基本上，每三四只 ETF 就有一只会消亡，而且它们现在“死”得越来越年轻。所以很值得来翻一翻：第一，哪些引起了我们的注意？有没有哪些我们觉得本该活下来却没活下来的？能看到哪些趋势？这本身就很有意思。另外，有没有哪些会被重新“挖出来”、像拉撒路（Lazarus）那样复活？

turns.en: We have seen that and done episodes about it. All right.
turns.zh: 这种情况我们见过，还专门做过节目。好的。

turns.en: And I found one of those, by the way. So anyway, yeah, I like doing this. I like grave digging, Joel.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，我还真找到了这样一个（复活的）例子。总之，是啊，我喜欢做这个。乔尔，我喜欢“挖坟”。

turns.en: We'll see what gems lie in that there cemetery. Joining us for our trip through the cemetery, Todd Sohn, Chief ETF Strategist with Baird Stratikas, as well as Andre Yap, a Senior ETF Research Associate with Bloomberg Intelligence. This time on Trillions.
turns.zh: 我们来看看那片墓地里埋着哪些“宝藏”。陪我们一起逛墓地的嘉宾有：Baird Strategas 首席 ETF 策略师托德·索恩（Todd Sohn），以及彭博行业研究（Bloomberg Intelligence）高级 ETF 研究专员安德烈·亚普（Andre Yap）。本期 Trillions——

turns.en: ETF Graveyard.
turns.zh: ETF 墓地。

turns.en: Todd, Andre, welcome back to Trillions.
turns.zh: 托德、安德烈，欢迎再次来到 Trillions。

turns.en: Thanks for having me.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们邀请我。

turns.en: Thank you. Okay, Eric, you walked us through how big the graveyard is in general. How big is the death rate this year?
turns.zh: 谢谢。好，埃里克，你已经给我们大致讲了这座墓地有多大。那今年的“死亡率”有多高？

turns.en: I have 182 officially liquidated. Now, there are some that are delisted, so it's a little bigger than that. We'll probably end the year 250 maybe. A couple things that stuck out for me just real quick. A lot of ESG. Schwab closed their ESG. And if Schwab closes it, you know it ain't selling. Because Schwab could sell ice to Eskimos. They've got like hundreds of millions of clients or whatever. So that's one thing. A lot of ESG closures, which I called a long time ago before it was cool. I'm not surprised about that. A lot of 2X stock ETFs closing that are babies. Basically like Trader, T-Rex, Defiance. Launched it. Like, for example, they launched the 2X Apple. Nobody cared. Closed it. Just boom, boom, real quick. And there was a good dose of crypto. Some of the sort of like, not Bitcoin, but like the really sort of like outer layer planet Pluto type crypto, like a Dogecoin ETF. A lot of equity. And then there was a couple unique ones in there that I'll save for the rest of the conversation. But that was my general take on it. There were a couple that returned a lot that still closed and a couple with decent assets that still closed. But largely all of them like were just complete duds.
turns.zh: 我统计到正式清盘的有182只。另外还有一些已经退市的，所以实际数字比这更大。到年底可能会达到250只左右。有几件事让我印象特别深刻，快速说一下。很多是 ESG 基金。嘉信（Schwab）把他们的 ESG 基金关了。如果连嘉信都关掉，你就知道它根本卖不动。因为嘉信能把冰卖给爱斯基摩人，他们有几亿客户之类的。这是一点。大量 ESG 基金清盘——这个我很早就预言过，那时还没流行，所以我一点都不意外。还有很多是刚“出生”的2倍杠杆个股 ETF 清盘了，基本上就是 Tradr、T-Rex、Defiance 这些发行商。他们发行，比如发了一只2倍做多苹果的 ETF，没人搭理，然后就关掉，砰、砰，非常快。还有相当一批加密货币基金。有些不是比特币那种，而是非常外围、像冥王星那种边缘加密货币，比如狗狗币 ETF。还有很多股票型基金。另外还有几只比较独特的，我留到后面再讲。这就是我的总体看法。其中有几只回报率很高却还是清盘了，还有几只资产规模不错也照样清盘。但大体上，它们几乎全是彻头彻尾的失败品。

turns.en: How does that closure rate compare with average? Because we have seen a lot of launches, Andre, but how do these closures compare?
turns.zh: 这个清盘率和历史平均水平相比如何？因为我们看到今年发行了很多新基金，安德烈，但这些清盘情况相比起来怎么样？

turns.en: Yeah, so we're on track to actually break the record to be the largest year for closures in 2026. We have two months left in the year and we're tied for third with 245 closures. So go team, let's go get that record.
turns.zh: 是的，我们正走在打破纪录的路上——2026年将成为清盘数量最多的一年。今年还剩两个月，我们目前以245只清盘并列历史第三。所以，加油啊团队，去把那个纪录拿下吧。

turns.en: All right, Todd, take us into the graveyard. Which headstone are you going to take us to first?
turns.zh: 好，托德，带我们进墓地看看。你要先带我们去哪座墓碑前？

turns.en: I went through the 200 or so, trying to find what caught my eye. Yeah, there's a lot of leverage, as we were talking about. The ones that really stuck out to me because I thought they were unique products, and as someone who looks at the markets through the lens of ETFs, I was disappointed to see them go. And that's the BondBlock's High Yield Sector Suite. And so what BondBlock's did.
turns.zh: 我把这200来只都过了一遍，想找出让我眼前一亮的。是的，就像我们刚说的，有很多杠杆产品。真正让我印象深刻的那几只，是因为我觉得它们是独特的产品；作为一个习惯透过 ETF 视角观察市场的人，看到它们消失我很失望。那就是 BondBloxx 的高收益债行业系列。BondBloxx 当时做的事情是——

turns.en: What was that ticker?
turns.zh: 那几只的代码是什么？

turns.en: Well, there's a few of them.
turns.zh: 嗯，有好几只。

turns.en: RIP?
turns.zh: “安息”（RIP）？

turns.en: RIPXYHE, or XHY, sorry. X, H, Y, F, X, H, Y, H, right? That's health energy, financials, healthcare, X, H, Y, I for industrials and so on. What they did was they took the high yield space and split it up by sectors to get more precise. And if you, you know, the high yield indices, they can be overweight telecom at some points, they can be overweight energy. You don't want that exposure and want to play more direct, but I guess it didn't catch on. And I was disappointed to see that go because it was a great way to look into what is going on in the high yield space, especially today. with hyperscaler debt being under pressure.
turns.zh: “安息”什么呀，是 XHY……抱歉。是 X、H、Y、F，X、H、Y、H，对吧？后缀 F 代表金融，H 代表医疗保健，I 代表工业，等等。他们做的是把高收益债领域按行业拆分开来，好更精准。你知道，高收益债指数有时候会超配电信，有时候会超配能源。如果你不想要那种敞口、想更直接地下注——但我想它没能火起来。看到它消失我很失望，因为它是观察高收益债领域动态的绝佳工具，尤其是在今天，超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）的债务正承压的时候。

turns.en: That's also interesting that it, you can't apply everything that works in equities to bonds. Cause I always think there should be thematic, but if these close, no wonder there's not thematic. Cause you've got to get a sector going first before you do themes. But the bond world is just not as fun. Like people don't want to have any fun over there. It's just like, Hey, just the facts, ma'am. Like I just want to get like, um, ag, different asset classes or durations and like.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，在股票上行得通的东西，并不是都能照搬到债券上。因为我一直觉得债券也该有主题型产品，但如果连这些行业型产品都清盘了，那没有主题型也就不奇怪了。因为你得先让某个行业跑起来，才谈得上做主题。但债券世界就是没那么好玩，那边的人好像压根不想找乐子。就像那句老话：“女士，我只讲事实。”我就是想拿到，嗯，不同的资产类别或者久期之类的，然后……

turns.en: Move on with my life.
turns.zh: 然后继续过我自己的日子。

turns.en: Um, just, Welcome to the graveyard.
turns.zh: 呃，总之，欢迎来到墓地。

turns.en: I know, another sign. At least they tried. Someday, the ETF market could be that big where I think they'll try the sectors and they'll finally work.
turns.zh: 我知道，又一个信号。至少他们尝试过了。总有一天，ETF 市场会大到那种程度，到那时我觉得他们会再试行业型产品，而且最终会成功。

turns.en: It could be a Lazarus.
turns.zh: 它可能会成为一个“拉撒路”（复活）案例。

turns.en: Yeah, that's a Lazarus candidate in my opinion.
turns.zh: 是啊，在我看来它是个复活的候选者。

turns.en: Andre, take us to the next tombstone of note.
turns.zh: 安德烈，带我们去看下一座值得注意的墓碑。

turns.en: So I'm going to play off Todd's sector themes and I'm going to go with the Westwood Engineered Beta Sector ETF. That's the WEBS ETF. Essentially, those are the equity counterpart to this. But instead of just being another Me Too sector ETF, they try to target volatility. So they would leverage up if their target volatility range was too low versus to their target. Or they would go to cash if they think that volatility is too high. And they launched 11 of them back in 2025. And every single one of them went in the graveyard this year.
turns.zh: 那我就接着托德的行业主题来说，我要讲的是 Westwood Engineered Beta 行业 ETF，代码 WEBS。本质上，它们是上述产品在股票端的对应版本。但它们不只是又一只“跟风”的行业 ETF，而是试图瞄准波动率。也就是说，如果当前波动率低于目标区间，它们会加杠杆；如果认为波动率太高，就会转入现金。他们在2025年一口气发行了11只。而今年，这11只无一例外全都进了墓地。

turns.en: So they're in good company. You know, they're not alone.
turns.zh: 所以它们算是“有伴”了。你知道，它们并不孤单。

turns.en: They have like their brothers and sisters beside them. So, you know, it's a family affair.
turns.zh: 它们旁边就是自己的兄弟姐妹。所以，你懂的，这是“全家福”。

turns.en: That's nice. But they all closed. It's kind of sad when it's the whole family, though.
turns.zh: 那挺好。但它们全清盘了。不过一整家都“走了”，还是有点伤感。

turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我知道。

turns.en: You don't want to be a survivor.
turns.zh: 你可不想当那个唯一的幸存者。

turns.en: You want to go with the crew.
turns.zh: 你宁愿跟大伙儿一起走。

turns.en: This is like Black Plague type stuff. Yeah, it's not friendly.
turns.zh: 这简直就是黑死病那种级别。是啊，一点不友好。

turns.en: Eric, take the flashlight and take us to another corner.
turns.zh: 埃里克，拿上手电筒，带我们去另一个角落看看。

turns.en: Crane Chair's Global Luxury ETF. When I travel around, I will get this question once in a while. Isn't there a luxury goods ETF? And I'm like, there's been like three or four attempts. This has been Lazarus'd. like four times.
turns.zh: KraneShares 全球奢侈品指数 ETF（KLXY）。我到处跑的时候，偶尔会被问到这个问题：难道没有一只奢侈品 ETF 吗？我就说，这类尝试大概有三四次了。这只基金被“拉撒路”式地复活过差不多四回。

turns.en: It'll probably be again.
turns.zh: 它多半还会再复活一次。

turns.en: I know. So we'll see. At some point, the luxury theme will work. I don't know when, and I don't want to the stars are aligned, but this thing was 69 basis points, only took in 2 million, but it's severely underperformed. So that's also an issue.
turns.zh: 我知道。所以我们走着瞧。总有一天奢侈品主题会奏效的。我不知道是什么时候，我也不想说“天时地利人和都齐了”，但这只基金费率69个基点，只募到200万美元，而且表现严重落后。所以这也是个问题。

turns.en: I got a grave next to that one, by the way.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，我这儿有一座紧挨着它的坟。

turns.en: Good segue. Next to the handbags, what do you got?
turns.zh: 转场转得好。紧挨着手袋（奢侈品）旁边，你带来的是什么？

turns.en: Speaking of luxury, there is the iShares US Consumer Focused ETF, IEDI. I was a fan of these. This was part of, I think, the Evolved suite they did years ago, where they tried to kind of mix up the GIX sector with their own classification. So it was going to be, I believe, something like Apple was in there, right? Eric and I just got new iPhones. We spent a nice chunk of our wallet on it. Apple is a tech company by GIX, but by this measure, I believe, assuming it was in there, it was a consumer company. So BlackRock, iShares, they tried to shake up what is a real name in a sector now, right? Because the Some of these companies are crossing multiple boundaries, but it didn't catch on.
turns.zh: 说到奢侈品，还有 iShares 美国消费聚焦 ETF，代码 IEDI。我挺喜欢这几只的。我想这是他们多年前推出的 Evolved 系列的一部分，当时他们试图把 GICS 行业分类和自己的分类体系混合起来。所以里面应该，我记得，比如苹果就在其中，对吧？埃里克和我刚买了新 iPhone，为此花掉了钱包里不小的一笔。按 GICS 分类苹果是科技公司，但按这个标准——假设它确实在里面——它就是一家消费公司。所以贝莱德（BlackRock）旗下 iShares 试图重新定义“一家公司到底算哪个行业”，对吧？因为其中一些公司正在跨越多个边界，但它没能火起来。

turns.en: Where would Tesla be?
turns.zh: 那特斯拉会被归到哪一类？

turns.en: Probably in that U.S. consumer focus. But, you know, Netflix is not indiscretionary, but it's a consumer name.
turns.zh: 大概会归到那只美国消费聚焦里。不过，你知道，Netflix 并不算非必需消费品，但它确实是个消费类名字。

turns.en: Right.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Sounds a bit dramatic, right?
turns.zh: 听起来有点戏剧化，是吧？

turns.en: They closed the Consumer Staples Evolve, too. I mean, I don't know. Did any of the Evolve make it?
turns.zh: 他们把 Evolved 系列的必需消费品那只也关了。我是说，我也不知道。Evolved 系列里有哪只活下来了吗？

turns.en: I think tech is the only one left.
turns.zh: 我想科技那只是唯一剩下的。

turns.en: Yeah. Interesting.
turns.zh: 是啊。有意思。

turns.en: But they had Staples Healthcare, right? Like Managed Care Plus Toothpaste.
turns.zh: 但他们有必需消费和医疗保健那几只，对吧？就像是“医保管理+牙膏”的组合。

turns.en: Yeah, I remember those coming out. They were kind of like an answer to something. I think they were an answer to ARK. They were like, okay, we're going to make these more crossed gig sector things. Because ARK, when ARK came out, I think what it really showed people is gig sectors are a little rigid. And ARK was like, we'll give you innovation across two or three sectors. And that was a big deal. And everybody followed. And they realized, okay, wait, maybe gig sectors need to be updated. And I think that's when that came out. Then there was an explosion of theme ETFs, and there was just so much competition.
turns.zh: 是啊，我记得它们推出的时候。它们某种程度上是对某种东西的回应，我想是对 ARK 的回应。它们的意思大概是：好，我们要做这些跨越 GICS 行业的产品。因为 ARK——当 ARK 出来时，我想它真正让大家看到的一点是：GICS 行业分类有点僵化。ARK 说，我们要给你横跨两三个行业的创新主题。那可是件大事，所有人都跟风。然后大家意识到：好，等等，也许 GICS 行业分类需要更新了。我想 Evolved 系列就是那时候出来的。接着主题型 ETF 大爆发，竞争实在太激烈了。

turns.en: Took it away.
turns.zh: 把风头都抢走了。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: One that I sorted by, and I thought this was interesting, the largest fund to close so far this year, Victory Shares West End Economic Cycle Bond ETF, BMDL. Anybody? Is there anything for being a big guy and falling on this list?
turns.zh: 我按某个维度排了一下序，觉得这个很有意思：今年迄今清盘的最大一只基金——VictoryShares West End Economic Cycle Bond ETF，代码 BMDL。有人知道吗？作为榜单上的“大块头”，它清盘有没有什么说法？

turns.en: No, nothing on there.
turns.zh: 没有，上面没有任何信息。

turns.en: Mystery. Just a death in the woods. Yeah.
turns.zh: 一桩谜案。就像“林中的一桩死亡”。是啊。

turns.en: I want to say there was a $ 400 million ETF that closed one time. I think iShares closed alts, and that was pretty big. And somebody closed a commodity ETF. So that's not the largest closure ever, but anything over $ 50 million to me would be eyebrow-raising. Like, well, why would you close it? They must have their reasons. That said, $ 100 million is not that big of a deal, especially if you're a company that has billions.
turns.zh: 我记得曾经有一只4亿美元的 ETF 清盘过。我想 iShares 关掉过几只另类投资基金，那次规模挺大。还有某家关掉过一只商品 ETF。所以这（BMDL）并不是史上最大规模的清盘，但对我来说，任何超过5000万美元的清盘都会让我挑眉：嗯，你为什么要关掉它？他们肯定有自己的理由。话虽如此，1亿美元其实也算不上什么大事，尤其如果你是一家管理着数百亿美元的公司。

turns.en: Which is what we're saying. Most of the ones that we're talking about here are much smaller than that. So this really comes down to, did you get assets or not?
turns.zh: 这正是我们要说的。我们这里谈论的大多数基金规模都比那小得多。所以归根结底就是：你到底募到资产了没有？

turns.en: Not really. So there are some flows, but when you look at flows and you see just a random big giant bar and you see nothingness for months, that's BYOA. That is a line.
turns.zh: 基本没有。所以是有一些资金流入，但当你看资金流的时候，只看到一根莫名其妙的大柱子，然后连续几个月一片空白，那就是 BYOA。那是一条（几乎为零的）直线。

turns.en: Bring your own assets.
turns.zh: BYOA——“自带资产”（Bring Your Own Assets）。

turns.en: Yeah, that's some in-house flow. Organic grassroots hits look like an uneven mix of like, it just looks more human and uneven. So this just looks like they had no actual interest beyond their own people. And that's probably why they closed.
turns.zh: 对，那就是些内部资金流入。真正有机的、草根式的热度，看起来会是参差不齐的组合，就是更“有人味”、更不均匀。所以这只看起来就是——除了自己人以外，根本没有真正的外部兴趣。这大概就是它们清盘的原因。

turns.en: It.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: I'm curious, any particular themes that tanked? We talked about bonds a little bit. There's some more fixed income than not in here. Any other one?
turns.zh: 我很好奇，有没有哪些特定主题崩得特别惨？我们稍微聊了聊债券，这里面固定收益类的还不少。还有其他主题吗？

turns.en: Let's go with leverage. So we spoke about this at the beginning, but leverage is just something that just seems to be the kind of useless calories that are just easy to get to. You eat them and you get rid of them really quickly. And that seems to describe leverage ETFs this year. We've had 93 of them close in so far this year.
turns.zh: 那就说杠杆吧。我们开头就提到过，但杠杆这种东西，看起来就像那种唾手可得的“无用卡路里”——你吃下去，很快又消耗掉。这似乎正好形容了今年的杠杆 ETF。今年迄今已有93只杠杆 ETF 清盘。

turns.en: 93 out of 245.
turns.zh: 245只里占了93只。

turns.en: That's about 35% of the closures or something about there. My math is probably bad, but forgive me. So that's Pretty big. Like if you work it out, we've had about 27 closures every month. Leverage is responsible for about 10 of them every month.
turns.zh: 大约占清盘总数的35%上下。我数学可能不太好，请见谅。所以这个比例相当大。如果你算一下，我们每个月大约有27只清盘，其中杠杆产品每月就贡献了大约10只。

turns.en: So without leverage.
turns.zh: 所以，如果没有杠杆的话。

turns.en: We'd have 17 closures every month instead of 27. So let's look at leverage as kind of the failing theme for the year.
turns.zh: 那我们每月的清盘数就会是17只，而不是27只。所以，我们可以把杠杆看作是今年最“失败”的主题。

turns.en: I guess. But it's also like been there for some really big moments, right? So it's sort of like either you hit it and you find something that traders really want or not.
turns.zh: 我想是吧。但它也曾在一些真正重大的时刻大放异彩，对吧？所以这有点像：要么你踩中了、找到了交易员真正想要的东西，要么就没有。

turns.en: Easy come, easy go.
turns.zh: 来得快，去得也快。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah, this is like the lottery for issuers. Because if you just get, let's say you launch 10, you get one or two to stick, you charge 1%, you're golden. So those eight were worth it. So this is the slickest spaghetti, the least likely to stick.
turns.zh: 是啊。是啊，这对发行商来说就像买彩票。因为，比方说你发行10只，只要有一两只站稳了，你收1%的费率，你就赚翻了。所以那（失败的）八只也是值得的。这就是那种甩出去最难粘住墙的“意大利面”（意指成功率最低的尝试）。

turns.en: Not everything needs leverage, but I get it. Just throw it out there.
turns.zh: 不是每样东西都需要加杠杆，但我理解。就是先扔出去试试。

turns.en: Most of these look like they're 2x stock.
turns.zh: 这些里面大部分看起来都是2倍杠杆个股 ETF。

turns.en: It's interesting.
turns.zh: 有意思。

turns.en: One of them is a 2x short micro strategy, which I would have thought would have had a nice run there for a minute. But even those... Sometimes that one probably is the third or fourth. So with leverage also, if you're not the liquid one, it's kind of like Ricky Bobby, if you're not first or last. If you're not the liquid one in that category, there's really not much else you can do. It's like, I don't really care if you're cheaper. This is the problem Corgis has. They have a ton of 2X and they're cheaper, but that crowd doesn't care about fees. So it's just, are you the liquid one? So if you're third or fourth, the odds of making it as a 2X are really tough. I mean, it's really hard.
turns.zh: 其中有一只是2倍做空 MicroStrategy 的，我本以为它能风光一阵子。但即便是这种……有时候它可能只是同类里的第三或第四名。所以对杠杆产品来说，如果你不是那个流动性最好的，就有点像瑞奇·鲍比（Ricky Bobby）那句“要么第一，要么最后”。如果你在这个类别里不是流动性最好的那只，那你其实没什么别的可做。就好像，我不太在乎你是不是更便宜。这正是 Corgis 面临的问题：他们有一大堆2倍杠杆产品，而且更便宜，但那批客户根本不在乎费率。所以关键就在于：你是不是流动性最好的那只？如果你排在第三或第四，作为2倍杠杆产品想活下去的概率就非常渺茫了。我是说，真的很难。

turns.en: You see them like trying to innovate and do these weird things where it's like, oh, we're doing leverage on an options income ETF.
turns.zh: 你会看到他们试图创新、搞一些奇怪的东西，比如“哦，我们要在一只期权收益 ETF 上再加杠杆”。

turns.en: Let's do that.
turns.zh: “就这么干吧。”

turns.en: These combining of the strategies and nobody wants this.
turns.zh: 这种把策略叠在一起的东西，根本没人想要。

turns.en: Nobody wants this.
turns.zh: 没人想要这个。

turns.en: That said, I remember when they were filed and we were like 2x NVIDIA, like who needs that? And that's like what, five, six billion dollars, 21%. That's 60 million a month, a year in revenue. So, you know, they got the last laugh. It has worked out. There's, multiple over a billion. So this is, the 2X stock space, actually leverage in general, is, I don't, it's a place you don't get a ton of respect. You know, like in the industry, it's like, oh, it's almost like you're selling contraband, like you're selling cigarettes or something. But you can make a ton of money because, you know, Vanguard will never play there and neither will BlackRock, neither will Schwab. Like all the Walmarts of the world are not, they're going to leave you be. And so it's very seductive for the issuers to do that.
turns.zh: 话虽如此，我记得当初它们提交申报的时候，我们还说：2倍做多英伟达？谁需要那玩意儿？结果现在规模大概有五六十亿美元，费率1%。那就是一年6000万美元的收入。所以，你懂的，笑到最后的是他们。它确实成功了，有好几只规模都超过10亿美元。所以这个2倍杠杆个股领域，其实整个杠杆领域，是个——我不知道怎么说——你得不到太多尊重的地方。在行业里，就感觉，哦，简直像你在卖违禁品，像在卖香烟之类的。但你能赚一大笔钱，因为，你知道，先锋（Vanguard）永远不会碰这块，贝莱德不会，嘉信也不会。所有这些“沃尔玛”式的大玩家都不会来，他们会把这块地让给你。所以对发行商来说，做这个非常诱人。

turns.en: I think you'll see more culling of those lineups, but more piling into tech because that's where the assets are going. There's a 2X Starbucks. I'm drinking a pumpkin spice coffee right now. I don't need 2X of that.
turns.zh: 我觉得你会看到这些产品线被进一步精简，同时资金更多地涌向科技，因为资产正在往那里流。市面上有只2倍杠杆的星巴克ETF。我这会儿正喝着南瓜香料咖啡，可我不需要“2倍”的它。

turns.en: Yeah. I mean, when a stock gets hot like Micron, nobody cared until that got really hot. Now that's a big deal. So sometimes you set them all out and you hope like the soccer ball gets kicked over to that area and you're like, okay, now it's our day. I would say the more volatile and techie, the better chances you have. But there is a world There is a scenario where 2x waste management could be like the hot new thing, you know, because we found that that stock tends to go up when AI falls. Because it's like garbage is the opposite of AI.
turns.zh: 是啊。我是说，当某只股票像美光（Micron）那样火起来之前，没人在意它；等它真的火了，那就成了大事。所以有时候你把这些产品全都摆出来，就盼着足球能被踢到那个区域，然后你就想：好，现在轮到我们了。我会说，越是波动大、越偏科技的，你胜算越大。但也存在这样一种情形：2倍做多 Waste Management（废弃物管理公司）可能会成为当红炸子鸡，因为我们发现，当 AI 下跌时，这只股票往往上涨。因为垃圾（garbage）正好是 AI 的反面。

turns.en: Back to the graveyard.
turns.zh: 回到墓地话题。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: Are there any asset managers or issuers who had a especially rough go here?
turns.zh: 有没有哪些资产管理公司或发行商在这儿过得特别惨？

turns.en: I would say the 2x people stuck out. Trader, Defiance, T-Rex, and Bitwise. Bitwise closed like 9 or 10. A lot of like, they tried like crypto income. They went pretty wild and they have some good hits, but they probably, they launched a lot of stuff. So they culled their product line.
turns.zh: 我会说，做2倍杠杆那批人最显眼。Tradr、Defiance、T-Rex，还有 Bitwise。Bitwise 关掉了大概9到10只。他们尝试了很多，比如加密货币收益类产品。他们玩得很野，也有过一些不错的爆款，但他们大概发行了太多东西，所以精简了自己的产品线。

turns.en: Like the Dogecoin funds.
turns.zh: 比如那些狗狗币基金。

turns.en: Yeah, BWOW.
turns.zh: 对，BWOW。

turns.en: Rest in peace, doggy.
turns.zh: 安息吧，狗狗。

turns.en: I know.
turns.zh: 我知道。

turns.en: Was that this year? Yeah.
turns.zh: 那是今年的事吗？是的。

turns.en: BWOW.
turns.zh: BWOW。

turns.en: BWOW. Which, yeah.
turns.zh: BWOW。是啊。

turns.en: Sounds like a 1989 rapper.
turns.zh: 听起来像个1989年的说唱歌手艺名。

turns.en: Okay. Did anybody happen to note if there were any other golden tickers that died?
turns.zh: 好。有没有人碰巧注意到，还有哪些“神仙代码”（好记又妙的ticker）也“死”了？

turns.en: I got a top five ticker closed this year.
turns.zh: 我这儿有一个今年清盘的、能排进前五的好代码。

turns.en: Oh, really?
turns.zh: 哦，真的？

turns.en: Top five.
turns.zh: 前五级别的。

turns.en: Toke.
turns.zh: TOKE。

turns.en: Toke.
turns.zh: TOKE。

turns.en: You know, I love verbs.
turns.zh: 你知道，我就喜欢用动词当代码。

turns.en: I mean, walk us through it. Yeah.
turns.zh: 我是说，给我们讲讲它。好。

turns.en: So this is the cannabis ETF from Cambria. Cambria also rarely closes ETFs.
turns.zh: 这是 Cambria 旗下的大麻 ETF。Cambria 也很少清盘 ETF。

turns.en: Wait, your selling point with Toke is that it's both verb and noun? Yeah.
turns.zh: 等等，你给 TOKE 的卖点就是它既是动词又是名词？是啊。

turns.en: Yeah, and you know exactly what it does. Like, it just checks every box.
turns.zh: 是啊，而且你一看就知道它是干嘛的。它简直是样样都占了。

turns.en: Yeah. Like, moo.
turns.zh: 是啊。就像“MOO”（拟声、另一个动词代码）那样。

turns.en: Right. Yeah. So, hack. Those are, like, it's hard to get all of that in one shot. Toke came out a little late. Cannabis has struggled. Has some good runs, but it largely has been a bummer. And it's weird. I just, I didn't mean to talk like the dude right there, but that's just appropriate. It's a bummer, man. Anyway, $ 13 million. This one was not quite a pure play. It had some cigarette companies. It was trying to capture the theme. I think it even had beer in here. I think the idea was to get a wider cannabis economy. The idea was great, but it was the sixth one to launch. The problem with doing economy ETFs and not pure plays is when the thing gets hot, this would lag. This would do better in a sell-off. It's almost like a lower beta version of a cannabis ETF, but Usually people who want the cannabis ETFs, they want that quicker, faster hit higher.
turns.zh: 对。是啊。还有 HACK 之类的。要在一个代码里把这些全占上可不容易。TOKE 出来得稍微晚了点。大麻这个主题一直很挣扎，有过几波不错的行情，但大体上就是个“扫兴货”。说来也怪，我并不是有意要像个“嬉皮老哥”那样说话，但这词儿用在这儿正合适。老兄，真是太扫兴了。总之，规模1300万美元。这一只并不是纯粹的大麻标的，里面还有一些烟草公司，它试图捕捉整个主题。我想它甚至还包括啤酒股。它的思路是想覆盖更广义的“大麻经济”。这个点子很棒，但它是第六只发行的同类产品。做“经济主题”ETF、而不是纯粹标的的问题在于：当这个题材火起来时，它会跑输；而在抛售时它反而表现更好。它几乎就像是大麻 ETF 的一个低贝塔版本，但通常想买大麻 ETF 的人，要的就是那种更快、更猛、涨得更高的“上头”感。

turns.en: Saw what you did there.
turns.zh: 我看到你在那儿玩的双关了。

turns.en: That went up here high.
turns.zh: 这（high，既指“上头”又指“涨得高”）确实蹿得老高。

turns.en: Not bad. Can I bring up a blast from the past?
turns.zh: 不错。我能提一个“来自过去的回忆”吗？

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 可以。

turns.en: Another era.
turns.zh: 另一个时代的。

turns.en: Take us to the other corner of the graveyard.
turns.zh: 带我们去墓地的另一个角落。

turns.en: The iShares Future Metaverse. Oh, Metaverse. And the Fidelity Metaverse ETF. What happened?
turns.zh: iShares 未来元宇宙 ETF。哦，元宇宙。还有富达（Fidelity）元宇宙 ETF。它们怎么了？

turns.en: Isn't that crazy?
turns.zh: 是不是很疯狂？

turns.en: Well, it's called AI. We don't talk about the Metaverse anymore. We just talk about AI.
turns.zh: 嗯，现在它叫 AI。我们不再谈论元宇宙了，只谈 AI。

turns.en: No more metaverse. I think there's probably one or two still left over, but man.
turns.zh: 元宇宙没了。我想可能还剩下一两只，但天哪。

turns.en: The only one that mattered is the one that you changed the name of your company for.
turns.zh: 唯一真正“重要”的那个元宇宙，是那个让你连公司名字都改了的（指 Facebook 改名 Meta）。

turns.en: That too.
turns.zh: 那个也算。

turns.en: It is really wild. That was such a big word.
turns.zh: 真是太不可思议了。那可是曾经那么大一个热词。

turns.en: It was a moment.
turns.zh: 那是属于它的一个时代。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是啊。

turns.en: And we just don't talk about that moment anymore. Have you heard about our AI?
turns.zh: 而我们现在干脆不再提那个时代了。“你听说过我们的 AI 吗？”

turns.en: So that fits in the thematic area.
turns.zh: 所以这归到主题投资那一类。

turns.en: Of something that didn't work.
turns.zh: 属于那些没成功的主题。

turns.en: Okay. Todd, any other surprising closes or noteworthy.
turns.zh: 好。托德，还有其他令人意外的或值得注意的清盘吗？

turns.en: I think given the environment we're in, Global X interest rate volatility and inflation hedge never caught on. But we have interest rate volatility right now. Inflation, it depends, I think, who you're talking to. It's certainly here in New York City. So that just comes as a peculiar one. I understand if it doesn't have assets, it's hard to keep going. But just in the bigger picture of what we're all dealing with in markets, I found that to be curious.
turns.zh: 我觉得以我们所处的环境来看，Global X 的利率波动与通胀对冲 ETF 从没火起来，挺意外的。因为眼下我们确实有利率波动。通胀嘛，我想取决于你问的是谁，但在纽约市，通胀肯定是实实在在存在的。所以这只就显得很奇特。我理解，如果它没有资产规模，就很难维持下去。但放在我们所有人面对的市场大局里看，我觉得这只的清盘很奇怪。

turns.en: Andre, closing thought?
turns.zh: 安德烈，结束语？

turns.en: I think the winner of the closures for me would be Goldman. you'd think that with their acquisition of Innovator closing this year that they would have a large product line to close, but not really. They only closed three products as a result of that. So there was really just limited overlap. So it seems like their targeting was really good. So they closed their three buffer ETX, GBXB, GBXA, GBXC. I did that in the wrong order, forgive me. But that's the only three that they closed. And all they did was just say, hey, we got the Innovator lineup now. You could go to those buffers instead. So I think they were very smart with their acquisition, and it showed in their closures this year.
turns.zh: 我觉得在清盘这件事上，“赢家”会是高盛（Goldman）。你会以为，随着他们收购 Innovator 的交易在今年完成，他们会有一大堆产品线要关，但其实并没有。他们因此只关掉了三只产品。所以两边的重叠其实非常有限，看来他们的（收购）定位做得非常好。他们关掉了三只缓冲型（buffer）ETF：GBXB、GBXA、GBXC——我念的顺序不对，见谅。但他们总共就关了这三只。他们要说的不过是：嘿，我们现在有了 Innovator 的产品线，你可以转而买那些缓冲型 ETF。所以我认为他们这次收购做得很聪明，这也体现在他们今年的清盘情况上。

turns.en: All right, Eric, take us out of the graveyard. Final thoughts?
turns.zh: 好，埃里克，带我们走出墓地吧。最后有什么想法？

turns.en: One more would be Invesco minimum volatility ETF. It's minimum variance SPMV. This is ironic because this is some old school stuff here. Invesco had the low vol ETF, SPLV, huge hit. Then iShares followed with the USMV, which was a different way to do low vol. So Invesco was like, oh, okay. we need some of that too. So they tried to match iShares. Long story short, the whole low minimum vol complex has kind of died out a lot. It reminded me of currency hedging. I think the buffer ETFs really have hurt that category because why hope you get lower vol, probably get lower vol, lock in lower vol with buffers. So we have a note or a theme we call that buffer ETFs kill the low vol star. So that's part of our theme. And also it's just interesting with SPLV was The original, this was trying to basically battle the other Me Too. Yeah, a lot going on there.
turns.zh: 再讲一个，是景顺（Invesco）的最小波动率 ETF，也就是最小方差那只，代码 SPMV。这有点讽刺，因为这里头是些“老派”的东西。景顺当年有低波动 ETF——SPLV，是个大爆款。接着 iShares 推出了 USMV，用的是另一种做低波动的方式。于是景顺就想：哦，好，我们也得来点这个。所以他们试图对标 iShares。长话短说，整个低波动/最小波动这一板块已经大幅萎缩了。这让我想起货币对冲。我觉得缓冲型 ETF 确实重创了这个类别，因为：与其“指望”自己能获得更低波动、“大概”能获得更低波动，不如用缓冲型 ETF 直接“锁定”更低波动。所以我们有一份研究报告、或者说一个主题，就叫“缓冲型 ETF 扼杀了低波动之星”。这是我们主题的一部分。而且有意思的是，SPLV 是那个“鼻祖”，而这只（SPMV）基本上是在跟另一个跟风者较劲。

turns.en: I will still stand for lowball. I'm not giving up on it. I agree with the buffer thing. Because SPLV has no tech in this environment.
turns.zh: 我仍然会为低波动（low vol）站台，我不会放弃它。缓冲型 ETF 那点我同意。因为在这种环境下，SPLV 里根本没有科技股。

turns.en: That's it.
turns.zh: 就是这个道理。

turns.en: If you need equity.
turns.zh: 如果你需要的是股票敞口的话。

turns.en: SPLV just buys the least fall stocks. And you end up in the really boring sectors, like utilities and.
turns.zh: SPLV 只是买那些最抗跌的股票，结果你就落到了那些特别无聊的行业里，比如公用事业，还有……

turns.en: Dirt.
turns.zh: “土”玩意儿。

turns.en: It's a dirt index, basically. The boomers who. In a huge sell-off, SPLV would go down too. It just would go down less.
turns.zh: 它基本上就是个“土里土气”的指数。那些婴儿潮一代……在大规模抛售中，SPLV 也会跌，只是跌得少一点而已。

turns.en: Yeah, but the flip side of that is that when tech rises, it gets none of that, so it just lags so much every other time.
turns.zh: 是啊，但反过来看，当科技股上涨时，它一点都吃不到，所以其他时候它就远远落后。

turns.en: That's why it's dirt.
turns.zh: 所以说它“土”嘛。

turns.en: You've got to carry the dirt.
turns.zh: 你就得扛着这些“土”东西。

turns.en: All right, I'm going to go around the room one more time. We're going to talk about the thing. If there was one product on this list that you think has a decent shot of coming back and, you know, getting out of the graveyard. Todd?
turns.zh: 好，我再在座各位绕一圈，聊聊这个话题。如果这份名单上有一只产品，你觉得它有不错的机会“复活”、走出墓地，会是哪只？托德？

turns.en: How about the Advisor Shares Hotels ETF? That was B-E-D-Z.
turns.zh: AdvisorShares 酒店 ETF 怎么样？代码是 B-E-D-Z。

turns.en: I remember this from COVID days, I think.
turns.zh: 我记得这只，应该是新冠疫情那阵子的。

turns.en: Yeah, you know, like, still demand for travel.
turns.zh: 是啊，你知道，旅行需求依然存在。

turns.en: Mm-hmm.
turns.zh: 嗯哼。

turns.en: Maybe getting a little bit tougher because of rates in oil and whatnot now. But at some point in the future, those ideally will calm down. Good ticker. There's a proper way to do it.
turns.zh: 也许现在因为利率、油价之类的因素变得有点艰难。但未来某个时候，理想情况下这些都会平息下来。这代码起得好，做这件事是有正经方法的。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.en: The themes natural monopoly ETF. By the way, the ticker is CZAR. C-Z-A-R.
turns.zh: Themes 自然垄断 ETF。顺便说一句，它的代码是 CZAR，C-Z-A-R（“沙皇”）。

turns.en: Pretty good.
turns.zh: 相当不错。

turns.en: Pretty campy. But I do like this idea of wide moats. And I think monopoly is kind of an interesting way to name it. So I just, you know, maybe it won't be named monopoly, but I really like this idea of pricing power. So I could see something like that being resurrected.
turns.zh: 挺“浮夸”的。但我确实喜欢“宽护城河”这个理念。我觉得用“垄断”来命名还挺有意思。所以，你知道，也许将来它不会再叫“垄断”，但我真的很喜欢这个“定价权”的思路。所以我能想象类似的产品会被复活。

turns.en: And Andre, what do you got?
turns.zh: 安德烈，你呢？

turns.en: So I know I just kind of poo-pooed a little bit on leverage ETFs, but I actually think, you know, the ridiculousness of some of them kind of makes them something that would come back in the future. So I think the 2X agricultural commodity ETF, so that's C-O-R-X and W-H-T-X, that's 2X corn, 2X wheat. Might be a candidate for revival at some point in the future.
turns.zh: 我知道我刚才有点贬低了杠杆 ETF，但其实我觉得，其中一些产品的“荒诞”之处，反而让它们有可能在未来卷土重来。所以我认为是2倍杠杆农产品 ETF，也就是 CORX 和 WHTX，分别是2倍做多玉米和2倍做多小麦。它们也许会成为未来某个时候复活的候选者。

turns.en: Who knows?
turns.zh: 谁知道呢？

turns.en: Maybe we'll enter an apocalypse and food will be scarce and we'll care so much about it.
turns.zh: 也许我们会迎来世界末日，食物变得稀缺，到时我们会无比在意它。

turns.en: Let's go with that. All right. We'll leave it there. Todd, Andre, thanks for joining us on Trillions.
turns.zh: 就这么收尾吧。好，我们就聊到这儿。托德、安德烈，感谢你们做客 Trillions。

turns.en: Thank you very much.
turns.zh: 非常感谢。

turns.en: Thank you.
turns.zh: 谢谢。

turns.zh: 感谢收听 Trillions。下次再会之前，你可以在彭博终端（Bloomberg Terminal）、Bloomberg.com、Apple Podcasts、Spotify，或任何你喜欢收听的地方找到我们。我们很想听到你的声音，欢迎联系我们。Trillions 由 Magnus Henriksen 和 Keshav Pandya 制作，Amy Keene 是我们的执行制作人，Cheryl Brumley 是彭博播客（Bloomberg Podcasts）负责人。

turns.zh: 再见。
